q: Of the twenty regions, which produces the least wine, hemmed in by Alpine valleys?
exp: Valle d'Aosta's vineyards climb high Alpine slopes and its total output is tiny, so bottles rarely leave the region. Molise, Liguria and Basilicata are the other very small producers, and their order shifts from vintage to vintage.

q: Cinque Terre and Rossese di Dolceacqua belong to which coastal region?
exp: Liguria is a narrow crescent of terraced coast squeezed between mountains and sea. Vermentino and Pigato carry the whites, and volumes are small enough that little is exported.

q: The white wines of Soave are built principally on which variety?
exp: Garganega ripens late and gives a lightly nutty, lemon-toned wine. Trebbiano di Soave or Chardonnay may fill a minority share of the blend.

q: Corvina, Rondinella and Molinara form the traditional blend behind which red?
exp: Corvina leads and supplies the sour-cherry lift the style is known for. The same grapes handled in a lighter way make Bardolino on the shore of Lake Garda.

q: Grapes are laid on racks to shrivel for months, then fermented right out to around fifteen percent alcohol. Which wine results?
exp: Appassimento concentrates sugar, acid and flavour before fermentation even begins. Taking that sugar all the way to dryness is exactly what separates Amarone from sweet Recioto.

q: A basic Valpolicella is refermented on the drained skins left over from Amarone. What is the result called?
exp: Re-passing the young wine over that pomace adds alcohol, colour and texture. It was conceived as a way of making a fuller wine without the cost of full appassimento.

q: Which variety must dominate a bottle of Prosecco?
exp: The grape was formally renamed Glera in 2009 so that Prosecco could be protected as a place name rather than a variety name that anyone might plant.

q: A second fermentation gives Prosecco its bubbles. Where does that fermentation take place?
opts: In a cask under a film of yeast
exp: The tank or Charmat method finishes quickly and keeps the pear and white-flower aromatics intact. Long ageing on lees in bottle would replace them with bready character.

q: The senior Prosecco denomination covers hills between two towns north of Treviso. Which pair names it?
exp: Conegliano Valdobbiadene Prosecco Superiore is DOCG, and the steepest slope within it, Cartizze, is the most prized site of all.

q: Which Italian region built its modern reputation on precise varietal whites from Collio and the Colli Orientali?
exp: Friuli sits in the far northeast against the Slovenian border. Cool nights and a run of both native and international whites define what it does best.

q: Tocai Friulano had to be renamed after a dispute with Hungary. What appears on labels now?
exp: The EU reserved Tokaj for Hungary, so the region's signature white dropped the first half of its name. DNA profiling showed the variety is Sauvignonasse, also called Sauvignon Vert, and it has no relation to Furmint or to Tokaji.

q: German is an official language in the northernmost Italian wine zone. Which zone is that?
exp: Alto Adige, or Sudtirol, was Austrian territory until 1919 and labels often appear in both languages. Schiava and Lagrein are its historic reds.

q: Teroldego Rotaliano is grown on a flat gravelly fan in which region?
exp: The Campo Rotaliano lies north of Trento where two rivers meet. Teroldego is its deeply coloured native red and is grown almost nowhere else.

q: Which grape accounts for the red wines of Chianti, Montalcino and Montepulciano alike?
exp: Sangiovese is Italy's most planted variety. Its local clones and names, Brunello and Prugnolo Gentile, are much of what marks those three zones apart.

q: A black rooster on the neck seal identifies a bottle from which zone?
exp: The Gallo Nero is the consortium mark for the hills between Florence and Siena. Chianti Classico has been its own DOCG since 1996, entirely separate from the Chianti DOCG that surrounds it, and only Classico bottles carry the seal.

q: A Brunello cannot be released until the fifth year after harvest. How much of that time must it spend in wood?
exp: Two years in oak is the minimum, with further time in bottle before release and a full extra year for Riserva. Rosso di Montalcino is the younger wine from the same zone.
